label: <DEL> delimiter step, gated by identity of first token to recall
explanation: Fires almost exclusively at the <DEL> delimiter step (95% of activation mass; ~58% of delimiter steps are active), i.e. the step where the model must output the first original token. Whether and how strongly it fires depends on that first token (out_tok = orig(0)): delimiter-step precision is ~0.9 when the first token is b, w, 0, e, g, z (top activations are nearly all sequences starting with w or b), ~0.75-0.85 for m, o, q, t, a, and only ~0.2-0.4 for x, v, h, r, i, s, 1, f, d, c. Shorter sequences (L=3) fire at a slightly higher rate. A small residual (~5% of mass) occurs at the first copy step (recall_idx 1, input = first token), mostly weak. Never fires during the original-token phase (t < L) and essentially never late in the copy phase. A token-set refinement on the first token raises precision to ~0.78 but lowers recall, so it gives no F1 gain over the plain delimiter predicate.
